summary: a session on a step-bearing entry names the steps it finished in its record; `shipped` ships exactly those, the entry with its last step, and nothing where a commit names none
acceptance: a build session is shown the step tags its entry carries and names the ones it finished in the record it writes — the continuing note while steps remain, the note to plan when none do — `shipped` returns exactly those tags with the `work` entry's own when its last step is among them, a commit on a step-bearing entry naming no step ships nothing, and the records gate refuses a commit naming a tag the entry does not carry
tests: a continuing note naming finished steps ships exactly those and leaves the work entry in the queue
a note to plan naming the entry's last remaining step ships that step and the work entry with it
a commit on a step-bearing entry that names no step ships nothing
the records gate refuses a note naming a step tag the entry does not carry
the rendered build prompt names the step tags the assigned entry carries
pins: a park on a step-bearing entry ships nothing, whatever steps its note names
a finishing commit on a work entry with no steps ships that entry
notes: One reader for the named steps, taken by both the records gate and `shipped`: a second parse is the copy that drifts. One entry because the halves have no safe intermediate — a prompt inviting a partial finish while `shipped` still ships all would delete steps nobody did. The prompt reads the steps off the queue the tick already carries (`TickContext.pending`), and the derive prompt's "a step waits on that channel" leaves with the channel.
